facts.text: A tag-based proximity system detects electronic tags carried by people or vehicles rather than recognizing people or objects, and warns or stops when a tag comes too close.
facts.quote: A tag-based proximity system does not look for people and objects; it listens for a small electronic tag that each person or vehicle carries, and warns or stops when a tag comes too close.

facts.text: UWB (ultra-wideband) tags exchange very short radio pulses with a machine and measure distance from travel time, often to a few tens of centimeters.
facts.quote: UWB (ultra-wideband) tags exchange very short radio pulses with the machine and measure distance from the travel time, often to a few tens of centimeters.

facts.text: RFID (radio-frequency identification) tags respond when a reader is in range.
facts.quote: RFID (radio-frequency identification) tags are simpler badges that answer when a reader is in range.

facts.text: Magnetic-field proximity systems are common on underground mining machines and generate a shaped magnetic field whose strength is measured by a worker-worn receiver to determine proximity.
facts.quote: Magnetic-field systems, common on underground mining machines, generate a shaped magnetic field around the machine; a worker-worn receiver measures its strength and so how close the worker is.

facts.text: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection on earth-moving machines, includes an annex for electromagnetic transceivers used in tag-based proximity systems.
facts.quote: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection on earth-moving machines, has an annex for such electromagnetic transceivers [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Tag-based proximity systems are widespread in mining.
facts.quote: These systems are widespread in mining

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines the on-board interface through which a tag-based proximity device asks a machine to slow or stop.
facts.quote: the technical specification ISO/TS 21815-2 defines the on-board interface through which such a device asks the machine to slow or stop [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The United States requires proximity detection on underground continuous mining machines, with a rule that the machine must stop before contacting a miner.
facts.quote: The United States requires proximity detection on continuous mining machines underground, with a rule that the machine must stop before contacting a miner [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Detection by tag-based proximity systems does not depend on weather or light.
facts.quote: Detection does not depend on weather or light

facts.text: Position and message paths in tag-based proximity systems are comparatively easy to simulate and fault-inject.
facts.quote: position and message paths are comparatively easy to simulate and fault-inject [Chapter 1].

facts.text: An untagged contractor or visitor is invisible to a tag-based proximity system.
facts.quote: an untagged contractor or visitor is invisible

facts.text: Tags used by tag-based proximity systems can snag or be removed.
facts.quote: tags can snag or be removed

facts.text: Radio propagation around large metal machines is not validated in simulation for tag-based proximity systems.
facts.quote: radio propagation around large metal machines is not validated in simulation

facts.text: Tag-based proximity devices from different suppliers did not interoperate.
facts.quote: devices from different suppliers did not interoperate [Chapters 1, 4, 6, 7].

facts.text: Underground workers reported proximity systems shutting down vehicles from once a day up to 15 times per cut of coal.
facts.quote: Underground workers reported systems shutting down vehicles from once a day up to 15 times per cut of coal [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Tags can bound what perception has to prove because a tagged person is covered by a more certain detection mechanism.
facts.quote: Tags can bound what perception has to prove, since a tagged person is covered by a more certain mechanism

facts.text: Tag-based proximity systems address a different sensing problem from general obstacle detection.
facts.quote: they answer a different sensing problem from general obstacle detection

facts.text: No simulation-fidelity study of tag-based proximity systems was found.
facts.quote: no simulation-fidelity study of them was found [Chapters 1, 6].
